title: Noon sakinah and tanween: the four rules and izhar: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Qadr, Al-'Alaq 1 to 12 and the noon sakinah rules
source: Written for quran/y3 lesson 10 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Noon sakinah and tanween rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 10. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

head: Noon sakinah (نْ)
Tanween (ـٌ ـً ـٍ)
rows: Middle or end of a word
Only at the end of a word

keywords.def: a noon with a sukoon on it: نْ
a double vowel at the end of a word that sounds like an extra noon
saying the noon clearly, with no extra humming
the throat, where the six izhar letters come from

questions.q: Is it izhar? Look at «كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ» (112:4).
questions.a: Yes: tanween before hamza (ء), a throat letter, so the 'an' is clear.

questions.q: Rule hunt on the pupil PDF: circle every noon sakinah or tanween in Al-'Alaq 96:1 to 10, then tick the ones that are izhar. Today's rota group recites 97:1 to 3 to the teacher in turn.
Extend: write the six throat letters in order from deepest to nearest the mouth.
questions.a: ء ه (deepest), ع ح (middle), غ خ (nearest the mouth)

questions.q: Stretch: why is there no humming in izhar?
questions.a: The throat letters are far from where the noon is made, so the noon is said clearly with no ghunnah.

questions.q: In «مِنْ عَلَقٍ» the next letter is 'ayn (ع). Which rule is it?
questions.a: A) Izhar: say the noon clearly. 'Ayn is one of the six throat letters, so the noon is said clearly. Ikhfa and iqlab need other letters.

questions.q: Think again: If you whisper 'min ahli' and then 'min-n-n ahli', which sounds clearer? Why do you think clear matters in the Qur'an?
questions.a: Clear speech keeps the meaning right. Before the throat letters the noon is said clearly: that is izhar.
